precepts.text: Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. There is no healing without confession. You can't cherry-pick what you want out of the Bible and expect to be received of God.
precepts.point: The first step of changing is to acknowledge that we have issues.

note.label: Pay The Price: Pleasure Now Regret Later

precepts.why:
The Pharisees asked, “Why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners?” Why is Christ sitting and communicating with ungodly people? To bring them to repentance. That was the whole purpose: “I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.” So if you think you're right, then he's not here for you. The first step of changing is to acknowledge that we have issues.

James shows that first step: “Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed.” You have to confess your faults so that we can pray for you and you can be healed. There is no healing without confession.

You can't cherry-pick what you want out of the Bible and expect to be received of God and Christ. Christ said, I came for the sick, those that need healing. But the sick have to own that they are sick. Many people are right in their own eyes; we don't want to see ourselves in a negative light and we act like the parts of us that aren't right will be all right with God. We will fall short of the kingdom if we keep that mindset of not changing.

So confession is where the physician's work begins. The one who acknowledges his faults can be prayed for and healed; the one who hides them, looking the part with fringes and a beard, stays sick.

precepts.text: He sent his word, and healed them, and delivered them from their destructions. You men know what the will of God is; then you're ahead of the whole world. His word is what's going to heal.
precepts.point: The first step of changing is to acknowledge that we have issues.

note.label: Pay The Price: Pleasure Now Regret Later

precepts.why:
Christ said, “They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.” He came for the sick, those that need healing. So what do we use to heal ourselves? The psalm answers: “He sent his word, and healed them, and delivered them from their destructions.”

He sent his word down to heal them. Write that down. The word of God is the medicine the physician brings.

So, men, do you know what the will of God is? Then you are ahead of the whole world, because people out here are crazy. People think you can still eat pork, or whatever you do, vote for Trump, whatever people are doing in this world. But you know his word, and his word is what is going to heal.

That is how the sinners at Christ's table were to be made whole: not by sacrifices, but by receiving the word he sent and letting it deliver them from their destructions. We all come in here sick, and we need to get cured.

precepts.text: They are cured with his word. That's why Christ said, I came for the sick, and I'm going to give them my word so they can be healed and cured.
precepts.point: The first step of changing is to acknowledge that we have issues.

note.label: Pay The Price: Pleasure Now Regret Later

precepts.why:
Ezra speaks of God “being judge”, and of those “that are cured with his word.” Cured with his word: that is why Christ said, I didn't come for the righteous, I came for the sick, and I am going to give them my word so they can be healed and cured.

Read on and Ezra shows what would happen if God did not forgive those who are cured by his word and put out the multitude of contentions: “There should be very few left peradventure in an innumerable multitude.” Out of all the multitude, hardly any would be left.

So the word of God will cure you; it will heal you. When James says, confess your faults one to another and pray for one another that you may be healed, we have to apply the word of God. That is the cure the physician gives to sinners.

And that is the meaning of “I will have mercy, and not sacrifice.” We used to give sacrifices to absolve us for the sins we committed, but that is not how it was supposed to be from the beginning. The Lord said, I want to see you change rather than keep on sacrificing. His mercy is for those who are cured with his word and actually change.

precepts.text: They that be whole need not a physician; I will have mercy and not sacrifice; I am come to call sinners to repentance.
precepts.point: The Pharisees asked why Christ ate with publicans and sinners, the same spirit as the Pharisee in Luke 18. They that be whole need not a physician: the law is not made for the righteous but for the sick, the lawless and whoremongers. I will have mercy and not sacrifice, from Hosea, and I am come to call sinners to repentance.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.why:
Manasseh says, “thou wilt save me, that am unworthy, according to thy great mercy.” Christ came for exactly such as him. “And when the Pharisees saw it, they said unto his disciples, Why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners?” It is the same spirit as the Pharisee in Luke 18: I’m more righteous than this publican over here.

“But when Jesus heard that, he said unto them, They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.” That is exactly what Manasseh said: the just need no repentance. The sick are the ones the law is made for, the lawless and the whoremongers.

“But go ye and learn what that meaneth”: go learn what that means, you guys are stupid. “I will have mercy, and not sacrifice.” He is quoting Hosea. God cares about mercy more than sacrifice. “For I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”

God is the God of those that repent. Manasseh had no sacrifice that could cover him under the law, but he found mercy, because Christ came to call sinners like him to repentance.

precepts.text: A captain's precept. Christ was moved with compassion because the multitudes fainted and were scattered as sheep having no shepherd. That is what motivates leaders to deny themselves the riches and the women and rebuild the nation.
precepts.point: Let the sisters get counsel from sisters. When you do give counsel, it must be what God wants them to hear and beneficial to them, not to your own wants.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
“But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.” As Christ went out teaching, healing and doing miracles, he looked and saw that his people fainted. They were out in the streets, they did not worship their God, and their own leaders were taking advantage of them at that time.

It is the same in this captivity as in the time of Rome. Look at our people out there: they are lost, they have no shepherd, they are confused. Not only have the people of the world taken advantage of us, but our own people take advantage too, using the knowledge to get preeminence.

So leaders are motivated because we see the same thing Christ saw: our people afflicted, with no leaders, and looking for a shepherd, which is Christ ultimately. Instead of benefiting ourselves, we see the decayed state of our people and make the sacrifices. To hell with the riches, to hell with the women, having sex, and all those other things. We do whatever it takes to rebuild our nation, so that we can truly benefit from each other and have one shepherd rule over us, with nobody able to take advantage of us.

That is the mind the Lord has put in us, and those who carry it are the ones standing in these last days, speaking with authority and showing our people: this is not the way; let us move according to this holy word and restore this nation. That is what it means to be the holy people God chose.

precepts.text: The harvest is plenteous but the labourers few; pray the Lord to send forth labourers, and keep working while He adds to you.
precepts.point: Day by day men came to David until it was a great host like the host of God. When the Most High works with you He sends help, as Christ said to pray for more labourers while continuing the work.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 12: The Tribes Gather to David

precepts.why:
Christ said, “The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few; Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.” Pray for more labourers, and keep working while He adds to you.

That is what happened to David. Captains of the thousands of Manasseh fell to him at Ziklag and helped him “against the band of the rovers: for they were all mighty men of valour”. “For at that time day by day there came to David to help him, until it was a great host, like the host of God.” When the Most High works with you, He sends help.

precepts.text: They that are whole need no physician; Christ came not to call the righteous but sinners to repentance.
precepts.point: Christ sat with sinners, but he was correcting them and showing them righteousness, not indulging their sin. We go to the streets to talk with sinners and give them the scriptures the same way.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“God judgeth the righteous, and God is angry with the wicked every day.” Yet every day you wake up, thank God for his son Jesus the Christ, because that mercy is holding back his fury and giving even those who disrespect Christ a chance to repent.

Christ showed that mercy: “They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick. But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”

Christ sat with sinners, but he was correcting them and showing them righteousness, not indulging their sin. He called them to repentance. We go to the streets to talk with sinners and give them the scriptures the same way, while God's anger with the wicked is held back by that mercy.

precepts.text: Go and learn what this meaneth, I will have mercy and not sacrifice, for I am not come to call the righteous but sinners to repentance.
precepts.point: Call upon the Most High in the day of trouble and he will deliver thee and thou shalt glorify him.

note.label: Psalm 50: The Mighty God Judges His People and the Wicked

precepts.why:
Christ said, “go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.” What that meaneth is written here in Psalm 50. The Most High takes no bullock out of Israel's house nor he goats out of their folds; every beast of the forest is already his, and the cattle upon a thousand hills. “Will I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?” Instead: “Offer unto God thanksgiving; and pay thy vows unto the most High”. He was doing away with animal sacrifice.

That is the mercy prophesied and brought into the New Testament. The Most High will have mercy and not sacrifice, and Christ came to call sinners to repentance. Call upon him in the day of trouble, and he will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify him.

precepts.text: Jesus knowing their thoughts said, Wherefore think ye evil in your hearts?
precepts.point: Many believed when they saw the miracles, but he did not commit himself unto them, for he knew all men, and needed not that any should testify of man: for he knew what was in man.

note.label: John 2: The First Miracle and the Cleansing of the Temple

precepts.why:
Many believed in his name when they saw the miracles which he did, but Jesus did not commit himself unto them, “because he knew all men, And needed not that any should testify of man: for he knew what was in man.” Matthew shows that in action: “And Jesus knowing their thoughts said, Wherefore think ye evil in your hearts?”

He knew their thoughts. Nobody had to tell him what a man was thinking; he knew what was in man, and he answered the evil in their hearts before they spoke it. That is why he did not commit himself to the many who believed only because of the miracles.

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

precepts.why:
Harvest literally means to gather the crops. “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired.” The nation not desired goes into Christ’s compassion on those that fainted and had no shepherd, stricken with misfortune.

“Before the decree bring forth, before the day pass as the chaff.” It keeps the language of the harvest. Chaff is the husk of grains and grasses separated during threshing. To pass as the chaff is to be destroyed, tossed to the side as good for nothing. That speaks first of the other nations and of those of our people that follow behind them and don’t repent before Christ returns, “before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you, before the day of the Lord’s anger come upon you.”

But gathered into what? We have to be gathered under structure and all the things we are doing. You don’t just gather together and wait.

note.label: These Are Not Defiled With Women Part 2

precepts.why:
Christ said it himself. “As Jesus sat at meat in the house, behold, many publicans and sinners came and sat down with him and his disciples.” The Pharisees asked, “Why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners?”

“They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.” If you say you are whole, you are saying you are not a sinner, that you have no sin in you, and then Christ did not come for you. We are a house full of sick people, a hospital. We all came here because we are sick and need healing, and the only healing is through the scriptures: the law is what is going to heal us, if you apply it. Don’t be a hearer only, be a doer.

The sisters came to be healed and the brothers came to be healed, so why would you want to destroy them? If you want to destroy them, you are saying you are not sick, and a man who is not sick does not go to the doctor. A brother who chases his woman down in the parking lot after catching her in the act has a sick spirit too. And many want to rush a brother or sister who is still on the operating table, with a broken spirit that has not had time to heal. When leadership says leave that one alone, it is not hating or blocking your blessing.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

precepts.why:
“Neither do men put new wine into old bottles.” The new wine goes into the commandments of God: that is the new man. When you are fashioned again anew, when you become a new creature, you have to put old things away, because the new can’t be kept in the old; otherwise it is no good. New wine in old bottles will not hold; the bottle is worn out, and it rips.

“Else the bottles break, and the wine runneth out, and the bottles perish.” If the body is not changed, it is not going to hold the commandments; it will not keep the commandments of God. If you are still in the world doing worldly things while keeping the commandments of God, you can’t serve both. Eventually it leaks out: after a while you are going to be offended, and you’re going to fall out. If you are going to be new, you have to be new all the way through.

“But they put new wine into new bottles, and both are preserved.” That is being born again: new wine in a new bottle. You keep the commandments of God, you are able to preserve the commandments, and you preserve yourself.

Come with receipts before you talk; the receipts of IUIC brothers are the passports, twelve countries for one young man, two or three books filled for the top leadership.

note.label: A Soul Without Purpose

points: He was moved with compassion because they fainted and were scattered abroad as sheep having no shepherd — no guidance, no leadership.

note.label: To Whom Much Is Given: The Burden and Beauty of Godly Leadership

points: We have to have the mind and spirit of Christ, and here is what moved him: “when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them.” Verse 35 says he was teaching in their synagogues, so these are Israelites. It is not compassion on the whole world, but on his people, because he will save his people from their sins, which is us.

“Because they fainted.” Think about how they fainted: alcoholism, drugs, whoremongers, fornicators, men not taking care of their families, lost in Christianity, lost in politics. When you are not living your true heritage you have fainted, because the real you is not alive, not conscious. Satan is in the driver’s seat.
“As sheep having no shepherd.” Christ saw a void of teachers and leaders with fire in their bones to teach their people the right thing, and he was moved with compassion.

Compassion is a feeling of deep sympathy and sorrow for another who is stricken by misfortune, accompanied by a strong desire to alleviate the suffering. The misfortune is the curses we are under. Deep sympathy and sorrow is them that sigh and cry in Ezekiel for the abominations they saw our people in, and Paul in Romans 9 wishing he could be accursed for what his people would go through. But compassion is more than sympathy. It compels you to do something for the stricken. Sympathy alone does nothing, like saying be warm and filled and never giving the food or the clothing. Hold on to that, because compassion is not far off from the fire that gets in your bones.

Our people are so lacking in compassion for their own that they are quicker to defend other nations; that is hatred for your brother. Sayings like don’t forget where you came from, and you can’t rise above the condition of your people, exist because of that lack of compassion.

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

points: “The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few.” We quote this a lot without thinking about what prompted him to say it. Compassion for our people is what should drive us to be laborers. There are so many of us, and a great work to gather our people, to help alleviate their misfortune, the curses, and to bring them light in the dark place where they reside.

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

points: “Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.” This is the call to labor that the rest of the class builds on.

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

points: Why does he call it a harvest? Because our purpose is to gather our people through his spirit, the spirit that gathered them in Isaiah 34. Just as God foreknew Jeremiah as a prophet to his people, he uses us to gather his people.

Gathering is not only everybody on the front line bringing people in. It also means keeping the same energy and zeal in the body. If people come in and see disorganization and strife not being addressed, the gathering fails. A congregation is like an emergency room: you will see sick people, but you should see treatment happening, not sickness fostered and allowed to grow. People have to be brought into something so they are filled with purpose, not just attendance.

It is like an ecosystem: everything relies on something else, and if the smallest part collapses, the whole thing collapses. From the brother who takes the trash cans out, to the one who lines up the chairs, to the one directing parking, if one is not in place we lose the effect of gathering. Many brothers are excited about teaching but not about anything else once the people are here, and one should not exist without the other.

To harvest is to gather, and you have to gather into a system. A fisherman who casts his net and leaves the fish rotting on the boat, never bringing them to shore or feeding the village, wasted his fishing. You have to be as on fire for those other layers as you are compelled to speak the word, though it starts with the compulsion to teach.

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

points: “Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.” You don’t just pray for it; in those prayers you are saying you will put your hand to the plow to help bring those laborers about, develop the men and bring something out.

Malcolm X, in his autobiography, had this same spirit Christ had when he saw them without a shepherd. He thought it outrageous that his small temple still had empty seats with the surrounding streets full of brainwashed brothers and sisters (insert fainted from verse 36) drinking, cursing, fighting and using dope. He called the recruitment attitude a self-defeating waiting view, the assumption that God would just bring more in. There should be no empty seats. The sisters’ response to everything on the internet is freaking twerking: you messed up my order, I’m going to twerk; you spoke to me nasty, I’m going to twerk. It’s disgusting, and that is the state of our people.

When we gather people into groups and only answer questions, we are not recruiting. Gathering is recruiting, like a military recruiter who stays on your ass until you enlist because he knows something will pull you away. We don’t want dead weight or seat warmers, on the brothers’ side or the sisters’.

The New York captains spoke of the same thing: why people have no sense of urgency, especially here in the West. Picture somebody chilling in slides or chanclas; you can’t hustle in slides, they fall off. That is the mentality, and not only in the West.

When we pray for more laborers, it is not only new people; it is the brothers and sisters already here maturing enough to put in the work. Where the hell are you? Especially you men: when are you going to get all your namby-pamby BS behind you and get the spirit of Jeremiah and the spirit of the disciples, so that we can gather more? Not ideas; anybody can get ideas. Brothers with zeal, fire, wisdom, purpose and compassion. God will not give the increase if he does not see us ready to facilitate the growth. Paul planted, Apollos watered, God gave the increase, but the work still has to be done. The three thousand souls in one day will come when we have the attitude right and the fire surging through each of us.

Malcolm said he had been impatient, and that is the spirit of Bishop Nathaniel from the beginning: not irrationally, but because of compassion and zeal that never ceases. We have a great cloud of witnesses in the scriptures and in our leaders. Some senior women have that fire too; sisters play a strong supportive role and should covet earnestly those desires, but far too few have it, and the same on the men’s side. Think of the white supremacist movements: those white women support the evil they do wholeheartedly. They are not lying in the cut doing nothing, quarreling among themselves; they have that same fire and zeal for wickedness. When are we going to see that with our sisters?

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

points: “Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few”. Some look at us and say there are a lot of them; the Bible says that is not enough. Israel is like the sand of the sea, and Christ said we are not going to reach all Israel.

note.label: BOLD WITNESSES FOR THE KINGDOM

points: “Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.” God is the Lord of the harvest. When you pray, pray for more labourers: that the Most High God send more brothers and put this spirit on more brothers to teach this word. Our people are dying out there and nobody cares about them except us. We are the labourers; that is the job of the leaders, the prophets.
